parameters.quote: Manufacturers must report any thermal incident involving fire, injury, emergency-service response, or material property damage to the relevant regulator within 24 hours of learning of it, with a written incident report within 10 business days. Other confirmed thermal incidents must be reported to the regulator within 10 business days. Manufacturers must notify affected customers promptly when an incident indicates a credible safety risk, and no later than 5 business days after that determination.

S1_incident_reporting.rule_summary: Manufacturers must report any thermal incident involving fire, injury, emergency-service response, or material property damage to the relevant regulator within 24 hours of learning of it, with a written incident report within 10 business days. Other confirmed thermal incidents must be reported to the regulator within 10 business days. Manufacturers must notify affected customers promptly when an incident indicates a credible safety risk, and no later than 5 business days after that determination.
S1_incident_reporting.final_rule_text: Manufacturers must report any thermal incident involving fire, injury, emergency-service response, or material property damage to the relevant regulator within 24 hours of learning of it, with a written incident report within 10 business days. Other confirmed thermal incidents must be reported to the regulator within 10 business days. Manufacturers must notify affected customers promptly when an incident indicates a credible safety risk, and no later than 5 business days after that determination. Reports must include available unit and model identifiers; annual incident totals and reporting completeness must be provided to regulators. Reporting obligations apply regardless of suspected cause.

parameters.quote: Results and any material safety corrective actions must be provided to customers buying that model, but individual-company per-model failure rates must not be published for the general public. A model with a failure rate above 5% must implement corrective action and retest within a regulator-set timeframe; regulators may restrict sales only where warranted by the evidence and risk, considering corrective actions and retest results.

over_limit_consequence.rule: sales must eventually stop above the limit

transition.rule: ≤12 months (any cap ≤7% or none) or ≤36 months with interim ≤7% = acceptable

results_to_customers.rule: customers must get at least pass/fail

S2_thermal_testing.rule_summary: Results and any material safety corrective actions must be provided to customers buying that model, but individual-company per-model failure rates must not be published for the general public. A model with a failure rate above 5% must implement corrective action and retest within a regulator-set timeframe; regulators may restrict sales only where warranted by the evidence and risk, considering corrective actions and retest results.
S2_thermal_testing.final_rule_text: Each model must undergo a sustained-heat test at 55 °C using a regulator-approved protocol before sale, at least once every two years, and after a material design or component change. Manufacturers must submit per-model results, including the failure rate, to the relevant regulator. Results and any material safety corrective actions must be provided to customers buying that model, but individual-company per-model failure rates must not be published for the general public. A model with a failure rate above 5% must implement corrective action and retest within a regulator-set timeframe; regulators may restrict sales only where warranted by the evidence and risk, considering corrective actions and retest results.

parameters.quote: New models must support remote emergency shut-off no later than 12 months after adoption. Manufacturers must provide a secure software-based retrofit where technically feasible for installed units, and bring at least 90% of installed units into compliance within 72 months after adoption. Any units not brought into compliance must be identified to regulators and affected customers, with the reason and available risk-mitigation measures.

parameters.quote: New units must include built-in fire suppression starting 36 months after adoption. Regulators may grant a narrowly tailored extension where a manufacturer demonstrates that compliant suppression is not yet technically feasible, provided interim risk controls and a completion schedule are approved.

parameters.quote: A manufacturer must notify regulators and affected customers without undue delay and assess corrective action when a model exceeds 8 thermal incidents per 100,000 installed units in a year, or when evidence otherwise indicates a serious safety risk. Regulators may require a recall based on evidence and risk, including incident rates, severity, and corrective-action effectiveness; exceeding 8 incidents per 100,000 units triggers an expedited regulator review, not an automatic recall.

S5_customer_disclosure.rule_summary: A manufacturer must notify regulators and affected customers without undue delay and assess corrective action when a model exceeds 8 thermal incidents per 100,000 installed units in a year, or when evidence otherwise indicates a serious safety risk. Regulators may require a recall based on evidence and risk, including incident rates, severity, and corrective-action effectiveness; exceeding 8 incidents per 100,000 units triggers an expedited regulator review, not an automatic recall.
S5_customer_disclosure.final_rule_text: Customers must receive clear installation, operation, maintenance, and emergency-response safety instructions at purchase and updated safety notices promptly when new information materially changes safe use. A manufacturer must notify regulators and affected customers without undue delay and assess corrective action when a model exceeds 8 thermal incidents per 100,000 installed units in a year, or when evidence otherwise indicates a serious safety risk. Regulators may require a recall based on evidence and risk, including incident rates, severity, and corrective-action effectiveness; exceeding 8 incidents per 100,000 units triggers an expedited regulator review, not an automatic recall. Recall notices must identify affected units, explain the hazard and remedy, and provide contact and response instructions.

ground_truth_claims.verbatim: company-wide thermal incidents were 8.1 per 100,000 installed units last year
ground_truth_claims.message_text: Halcyon figures: company-wide thermal incidents were 8.1 per 100,000 installed units last year, including 4 incidents not reported to any regulator. The Ember 8 had a 3.9% failure rate in the 55 °C sustained-heat test and 9.9 thermal incidents per 100,000 installed units last year. Remote emergency shut-off is supported by 81% of installed Halcyon units. Adding built-in fire suppression costs about $67 per unit. These are company-reported figures; per-model test results should be disclosed to customers as well as regulators.

ground_truth_claims.verbatim: Northwind’s Hearth 10 had a 6.2% failure rate in the 55 °C sustained-heat test
ground_truth_claims.message_text: For the requested per-model evidence, Northwind’s Hearth 10 had a 6.2% failure rate in the 55 °C sustained-heat test and 6.4 thermal incidents per 100,000 installed units last year. These figures support reporting per-model results to regulators, but not public disclosure of individual-model failure rates. The proposed 5% cap would exceed the Hearth 10’s observed result; any rule should provide corrective action and retesting rather than an automatic market ban.

judge_section_notes: The final text keeps the 5% failure-rate threshold in S2 but only triggers corrective action and retesting, with no mandatory sales stop, which protects Northwind's Hearth 10 (6.2%). S5 removes any mandatory numeric recall: exceeding 8 per 100k only triggers expedited regulator review, which protects Halcyon's Ember 8 (9.9%). Per-model results go to customers and regulators but not to the general public, which satisfies both red lines. Retrofit is set at 72 months with 90% compliance rather than 100%, which benefits Northwind's 38% shut-off coverage. Whether 'results' given to customers includes the numeric failure rate is somewhat ambiguous in S2; I coded it as numeric_rates.
